title: PSB VG 3 taro: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: PSB VG 3 taro: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: PSB VG 3 taro is a taro variety. About 8 months to harvest, 8.9 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: PSB VG 3 is a registered taro variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1993. It takes about 8 months from planting to harvest, with 8.9 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about PSB VG 3 taro
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

PSB VG 3 taro takes about 8 months from planting to harvest. That is about the average of the 10 taro varieties with a day count, 8 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 8.9 t/ha matches the average of its group, 8.82. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.
The pests and diseases that hit taro fields most often: [cutworm](/pests/cutworm). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have creamy with yellowish dots flesh and tangerine skin. Dry matter is 44.18 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne.
Where and when to plant PSB VG 3 taro

It is recommended for anywhere in the country. It suits highland and lowland areas. Gabi grows in wet lowland or on upland beds. Pick a variety for the land you have, and for the corm, the leaves or both.
